arrivee_ville.title: The Town of Smiles
arrivee_ville.text:
You arrive in town with Aikito.

The weather is nice.

The houses are pretty.
The people are dressed with care.

But something is strange.

Everyone is smiling.

The lady carrying bags that are far too heavy. Smiling.
The man whose bike has a flat tire. Smiling.
The little girl who just fell down. Smiling.

Aikito sits down next to you.

He tilts his head to one side.

**"These smiles don't reach their eyes."**

choices.text: Look at the people more closely.

affiche_cirque.title: The Poster
affiche_cirque.text:
In the middle of the square, a big poster announces:

**✨ THE GRAND PERFECT CIRCUS ✨**
*Where everyone is always happy*
*Tonight and every night*

Golden stars everywhere.
Smiling faces on the poster.

A man in a top hat is handing out tickets.

He is smiling too.
Very hard.
Too hard.

Aikito sniffs the ticket.

**"It smells like paper and sadness."**

choices.text: Ask the man what this circus is.

homme_billet.title: The Ticket Man
homme_billet.text:
The man looks at you with his big smile.

**"At the Grand Perfect Circus, everyone is happy!"**
**"No tears. No anger. No sadness."**
**"Nothing but happiness!"**

He says it very fast.
As if he were reciting a lesson.

You notice that his hands shake a little
when he holds out the ticket to you.

Aikito looks him right in the eyes.

The man looks away.

choices.text: Take the ticket and go in.
Ask him why his hands are shaking.

mains_tremblantes.title: Trembling Hands
mains_tremblantes.text:
The man stops smiling for a second.

Just one second.

**"I... I'm not shaking."**

He puts his smile back on very fast.

**"Everything is just fine! Come in, come in!"**

But you saw.
Aikito saw too.

He gives your hand a little nudge with his nose.

**"He's scared of something."**

choices.text: Go into the circus to find out.

entree_cirque.title: The Circus Entrance
entree_cirque.text:
The big top is huge and red.

Golden lights everywhere.
Cheerful music playing very loudly.

The people inside are all smiling.
They are looking at the ring.
They are clapping.

But nobody is talking.
Nobody is really laughing.

Just clapping.
And smiles.

Aikito pins his ears back.

**"Too much noise. Not enough joy."**

observer_public.title: The Audience
observer_public.text:
You sit down in the bleachers.

The little girl next to you is smiling.
But her eyes are red.
She cried before coming in.

The man behind you is smiling.
But he yawns non-stop.

The lady in front of you is smiling.
But she keeps staring at her shoes.

You lean toward the little girl.

**"Are you okay?"**

She looks at you, surprised.

Nobody has asked her that in a long time.

petite_fille.title: The Little Girl
petite_fille.text:
The little girl looks around.

Then she whispers, very loudly.

**"I don't feel like smiling today."**
**"But if I don't smile, the Ringmaster gets angry."**
**"And if the Ringmaster is angry, everybody is angry."**

Aikito walks over to her slowly.

He rests his head on her knees.

She looks at him.

And for the first time,
she really smiles.

Just a tiny bit.
But for real.

choices.text: Go find out why the Ringmaster does this.

clown_coulisses.title: The Clown
clown_coulisses.text:
Behind the red curtain, you find a clown.

He is sitting on the floor.
His orange wig is crooked.

He is laughing.

He can't stop laughing.

But his eyes, on the other hand, are not laughing at all.

**"Ha ha ha... I can't stop... ha ha..."**

Aikito sits down in front of him.
Very calm.
He waits.

The clown looks at him.
And stops for a second.

**"You don't smile."**
**"That's good."**

choices.text: Sit down beside him in silence.

secret_clown.title: The Clown's Secret
secret_clown.text:
The clown lowers his voice.

**"The Ringmaster says that if we stop smiling..."**
**"...people won't like the show."**
**"And if people don't like it..."**
**"...we won't have a circus anymore."**

He looks down at his big shoes.

**"So I smile."**
**"Even when my stomach hurts."**
**"Even when I'm tired."**
**"Even when I want to cry."**

Aikito licks his hand.

**"Your stomach knows the truth."**

choices.text: "People love you for you, not for your smile."

trapeziste.title: The Trapeze Artist
trapeziste.text:
You climb a few steps.

At the top, a young woman is sitting on her swing.
She smiles down at you.

But her legs are trembling.

**"I'm scared of the drop."** she says quietly.
**"I always have been."**

**"But the Ringmaster says a smiling performer"**
**"gives the audience confidence."**

Aikito barks once.
Gently.

She looks at him.

**"He's not afraid to tell the truth, is he."**

coulisses.title: Backstage
coulisses.text:
You walk through the backstage area.

Everywhere, performers are smiling in their corners.
But they stop as soon as they think nobody is watching.

A juggler frowning.
An acrobat sighing.
A musician stretching his shoulders.

Their real faces last two seconds.
Then the smile comes back.

Like a mask being put back on.

Aikito looks at you.

**"They forgot that masks are tiring."**

bureau_directeur.title: The Ringmaster's Office
bureau_directeur.text:
The Ringmaster is a tall man with a mustache.

He greets you with the biggest smile you have ever seen.

**"Welcome! Everything is fine here!"**
**"Nothing but happiness! Nothing but joy!"**

You look around.

On his desk, there is a photo.
An old circus.
People laughing for real.

Some of them have tears in their eyes from laughing so hard.

The Ringmaster notices you looking at the photo.

His smile trembles, just for a tiny second.

choices.text: "Why does everyone have to smile here?"

photo_directeur.title: The Photo
photo_directeur.text:
The Ringmaster picks up the photo.

He looks at it for a long time.

**"It was... my old circus."**

His voice changes.
Softer. More real.

**"People really laughed. Sometimes they cried."**
**"They were scared. They were surprised."**
**"Every feeling there is."**

He puts the photo back down.

**"But one night, nobody came."**
**"And I was afraid it was because they weren't happy."**
**"So I decided that everyone would always be happy."**

Aikito puts a paw on the Ringmaster's foot.

**"You were scared."** you say softly.
**"So you put a mask on everyone."**

question_directeur.title: The Question
question_directeur.text:
The Ringmaster stops.

His big smile trembles.

**"Because... because people come to be happy!"**

**"And if the performers are sad, the audience will be sad."**
**"And if the audience is sad, they won't come back."**

He says it very fast.
As if it were urgent.

Aikito sits down.
He yawns.
Calmly.

The Ringmaster looks at him.

**"He doesn't look happy..."**
**"And yet I want to pet him."**

grand_moment.title: The Truth
grand_moment.text:
The Ringmaster stays silent.

For a very long time.

Aikito goes to lie down on his feet.

The Ringmaster looks at him.
Then he looks at you.

**"The people came that night..."**
**"...even though it wasn't perfect."**

He looks at the photo again.

**"Maybe I was scared of nothing."**

He stands up slowly.
He takes off his top hat.

Underneath, his hair is a wild mess.

He smiles.

Not his big smile.

A small, tired smile.
But a real one.

scene_finale.title: On Stage
scene_finale.text:
The Ringmaster climbs onto the stage.

He takes off his forced, big smile.

He speaks to the audience.

**"Tonight... you have the right to be just as you are."**

Silence.

Then the little girl in the bleachers says:
**"I was sad earlier."**

Someone else says:
**"I was tired."**

And then everyone starts talking.
About their real days.
About their real feelings.

And something strange happens.

They smile.

For real.

Aikito wags his tail.

fin_principale.title: Ending — The Real Circus
fin_principale.text:
The clown takes off his painted smile.

Underneath, he is smiling anyway.
But for real this time.

The trapeze artist jumps.
She is still scared.
But she shouts as she jumps.

A real shout.
And the people clap even harder.

On the way out, the little girl catches up with you.

**"Thank you."** she says.
**"Nobody ever told me it was normal to be sad."**

Aikito looks at her.

**"Feelings are like the weather."**
**"They change."**
**"That's what makes them good."**

You nod.

Tonight, the circus was imperfect.

And that's why it was beautiful.

fin_clown_libre.title: Ending — The Clown's Laugh
fin_clown_libre.text:
The clown wipes off his makeup.

He has a normal face.
With the wrinkles of someone who has laughed and cried.

He looks at you.

**"I had forgotten how to do it."**
**"To laugh for real."**

He tries.

A small laugh.
A little rusty.

Then a bigger one.

Aikito barks with joy.

Tonight, the clown laughs for real for the first time in a long time.

And it is the best act in the whole circus.

fin_trapeziste_libre.title: Ending — The Trapeze Artist's Scream
fin_trapeziste_libre.text:
The trapeze artist climbs to the top.

She is trembling.

She jumps.

And this time she screams.
A real scream, from someone who is scared
and jumps anyway.

The audience is silent.

Then someone claps.

Then everyone.

She lands.
Tears in her eyes.

**"That was better..."** she says.

Aikito wags his tail again.

Being scared and showing it
is braver than pretending.

fin_partir.title: Ending — The Way Home
fin_partir.text:
You did not find the Ringmaster.

But as you leave the circus,
you run into the clown.

He is not laughing anymore.

He is looking up at the sky.

**"Lovely night."** he says.

**"Yes."** you answer.

You stay there for a minute.
Without smiling.
Without pretending.

Just two people looking up at the sky.

Aikito sits down between you.

Sometimes,
a minute of the real thing
is worth more than an hour of pretending.
